name: International standards (ILO)
sources: ILO General principles and operational guidelines for fair recruitment (2019)
note: Not binding law. Present as international standards, never as 'illegal'. Use when the country file has no matching rule, e.g. fees charged by an agent in the worker's home country.

rules.match_hint: worker or candidate pays a recruitment, placement, service, visa processing or medical fee to an agent or employer, in any country
rules.why: International labour standards say workers should never pay recruitment fees or related costs. These fees often trap workers in debt.
rules.action: Ask for the fee to be removed. Keep receipts of anything you paid. Check if the agent is licensed in your home country.

rules.match_hint: final contract given only on arrival, terms may change later, contract not in a language the worker understands
rules.why: Migrant workers should get a clear written contract in a language they understand before leaving home. A contract that only appears after arrival is a common way to swap the promised job or salary.
rules.action: Do not travel or pay until you have the final contract and understand it.

rules.match_hint: hours 'as per company requirement', job or location can change at any time, salary not clearly stated
rules.why: Your contract should clearly state where you will work, what you will do, and the conditions. Vague terms make it easy to change them later.
rules.action: Ask for the exact hours, job, location and salary to be written down.

rules.match_hint: agent or employer keeps the worker's passport, ID or contract
rules.why: Your passport, ID and contract should never be taken or kept by an employer or agent.
rules.action: Keep your documents yourself, or at least keep copies and photos of them on your phone.

rules.match_hint: worker needs permission to leave, change employer or go home, or must pay to leave
rules.why: Workers should be free to quit their job and go home, and should not need their employer's permission to change jobs.
rules.action: Before signing, ask what happens if you want to leave. Contact the hotline if you are being stopped.
